title: Launch of expanded Pennsylvania Amtrak service brings more travel choices through Norfolk Southern partnership
body_markdown:
This week, Norfolk Southern marked a major milestone in enhancing transportation options in Pennsylvania, joining federal, state and local officials to launch a second daily round trip of the Pennsylvanian Amtrak passenger train. The initiative, which was made possible by the partnership of the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT), Norfolk Southern (NS) and the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), expands passenger rail options across Pennsylvania while keeping freight moving along one of the commonwealth's most important rail corridors.


With its inaugural trip Nov. 18, Amtrak's Pennsylvanian service has doubled from one to two daily round trips between Pittsburgh and New York City, offering travelers more flexibility to connect with communities across the commonwealth.


**Top takeaways**


- The[Pennsylvanian,](https://www.amtrak.com/pennsylvanian-train) which runs largely on NS-owned track in the western portion of the state, now offers two daily round trips, giving travelers greater scheduling flexibility thanks to a partnership involving NS, PennDOT and Amtrak.
- Infrastructure upgrades along the corridor support expanded passenger service while preserving freight operations.
- This passenger rail expansion builds on NS' history as a key partner in smart, sustainable passenger rail growth. Over the past 15 years, NS has supported the launch of 12 new round-trip Amtrak services across its network — more than any other Class I railroad during that period.


**Why it matters**


For residents of Pittsburgh, Johnstown, Altoona and other communities along the route, another daily departure means more choice when planning a trip. The additional service strengthens connections to jobs, education and tourism across the commonwealth while preserving critical freight connections for businesses that rely on rail.


**Behind the expansion**


The Pennsylvanian travels on our rail line connecting Pittsburgh and Harrisburg. That same corridor is an important freight corridor connecting businesses with markets across the country.


[A 2023 agreement between NS and PennDOT](https://www.norfolksouthern.com/en/newsroom/story-yard/expanding-passenger-rail-access-in-western-pennsylvania--a-win-win-for-communities-and-commerce) laid the groundwork for the additional passenger service. Under the agreement, we are responsible for constructing and maintaining infrastructure improvements designed to accommodate more passenger trains while maintaining freight throughput. The planned work includes track, siding and communications signal improvements.


State and federal funding supports the improvements, with additional infrastructure work continuing beyond the service launch. The approach advances Pennsylvania’s passenger rail goals while supporting the safe and efficient movement of goods through the Commonwealth.


**What they’re saying**


“Norfolk Southern is proud to celebrate the start of Amtrak’s second daily Pennsylvanian round-trip, a milestone that represents a win for travelers, communities and businesses that rely on rail here in Pennsylvania. This expansion shows what public and private partners can achieve together, giving Pennsylvanians more transportation options while keeping freight moving safely and efficiently across the Commonwealth.” – **Mike McClellan, Norfolk Southern Chief Strategy Officer**


“Under Governor Shapiro’s leadership, PennDOT is aggressively putting additional federal and state transportation investments to work for Pennsylvanians, whether it’s fixing our roads and bridges or restoring and improving passenger rail service. Thanks to strong partnerships with Amtrak, Norfolk Southern, and communities across the state, this long-awaited expansion of service on the Pennsylvanian is now a reality.” – **PennDOT Secretary Mike Carroll**


“Doubling Pennsylvanian service fundamentally expands the way people connect to communities, jobs, education, and opportunities across the Commonwealth and beyond. This is exactly the kind of growth we want to deliver for our customers and the communities we serve.” – **Amtrak Interim President Byl Herrmann**


The full announcement can be read[here](https://www.pa.gov/governor/newsroom/2026-press-releases/gov--shapiro-celebrates-journey-of-2nd-daily-train-between-pitts) .


**A shared approach**


The Pennsylvanian expansion builds on our work with passenger rail partners to develop service that meets community needs and preserves the reliable freight service businesses depend on.
